senses: A person who advocates syndicalism.
Of a book: having a yapp.
Any of a group of butterflies of the subfamily Nymphalinae whose wings bear a checkered, spotted pattern.
A mechanical multiple musical instrument designed to sound like an orchestra or band.
ety: From German Orchestrion, from Orchester (“orchestra”) + -ion (compare Akkordion (“accordion”)). Developed by the German composer, organist, teacher and theorist Georg Joseph Vogler (1749–1814).

senses: The branch of chemistry that deals with the creation of the elements, and their isotopic distribution, in the universe; also with the synthesis and reactions of simple molecules in interstellar space.
Having a tendency to reject the plans or proposals of others.
The conversion of biological material into usable products; but especially the conversion of biomass into biofuel
Resembling the thrash genre.
An abrupt, damaging breakdown or failure.
A violent collision involving one or more vehicles.
An instance or the result of smashing; that which has been smashed into pieces.
examples: I discovered that a lot of imported drainage-pipes for the settlement had been tumbled in there. There wasn’t one that was not broken. It was a wanton smash-up.

senses: Any moth of the family Lasiocampidae.
ety: Alteration of egger, in reference to the shape of this moth's cocoon.

senses: formed by cliffs
examples: The cliffed coasts are cut mostly in consolidated rock of somewhat uniform material, which usually results in straight coastlines.
The abundance of cliffed coasts around the world reflects the major changes that have taken place between relative levels of land and sea in recent geological times.
In the case of a cliffed marsh edge, wave heights increase at the edge but are dissipated rapidly in the first 10-20m landward of the cliff.

senses: Queer, strange.
A lot of, very, great.
examples: I was after finishing my dinner when there was quare knock on the door.
Look, the quare fellow’s got to be buried in the morning, whether we like it or not, so cut the mullarkey and get back to work.
He'd brought a quare amount of money with him.

senses: Covered with scrub, trees, or rough or shaggy growth.
Jagged; having a rough, uneven surface.
Of hair: long; rough; shaggy.
ety: From Old English sceacgede, from sceacga (“hair”), from Proto-Germanic *skaggiją (“beard, stem”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kek-, *(s)keg- (“to jump, move, hurry”).

senses: One who shows extreme love and admiration for themself.
An egoist; a person full of egoism and pride.
ety: From Narcissus (“a character in Greek mythology who became obsessed with his own reflection”) + -ist.

senses: A sense of pleasure derived from listening to something, particularly music.
A sense of pleasure derived from the physical stimulation of the earlobe or ear canal, such as when using a Q-Tip to clean the ear.
examples: One lady in the audience said that when Robinson sings she just sits in her chair and has multiple "eargasms."
A sucker for the Q-tip eargasm, I scoffed at the warning on the box: "Do not use swab in ear canal."

senses: A tropical evergreen tree, Neolamarckia cadamba (syn. Anthocephalus indicus, Nauclea cadamba), native to South and Southeast Asia.
ety: Cf. Bengali কদম (kodom), corruption of Sanskrit कदम्ब (kadamba). Ultimately from Proto-South Dravidian *kaṭ-ampu (“Neolamarckia cadamba”).
examples: Kinaram made the elephant sit under a large kadam tree.

senses: A fish-eating bird (Anhinga anhinga) of the Americas with a thin, pointed bill and a long, thin neck.
ety: From taxonomic name Anhinga or Portuguese anhinga, from Old Tupi anhinga.

senses: A Shinto temple.
To change the pitch, intensity or tone of one's voice or of a musical instrument.
To move from one key or tonality to another, especially by using a chord progression.
ety: From Latin modulor (“to measure, regulate, modulate”) + -ate (verb-forming suffix), from modulus (“measure”). Compare module, modulus. By surface analysis, modul(e) + -ate.

senses: Part of a valley where the lower and flatter portion of the primary valley floor suddenly becomes steeper, used in computing a keyline for the efficient planning of water usage.
An important point in an image, used in computer vision systems when detecting objects etc.
An identifier for a point in time, especially within a digital recording; a timestamp.
examples: We use a deep convolutional neural network within an expectation maximization framework to take advantage of weakly labeled data like image level annotations or keypoint annotations.

senses: A railroad employee responsible for a train's brakes, couplings etc.
A person employed to work the steam engine or other machinery that raises the coal from the mine.
A lunar mansion in Hindu astrology; one of 27 (sometimes also 28) sectors along the ecliptic.
One to whom a thing is assigned.
One who is appointed to act or speak in place of another; an agent.
ety: From Middle English assigne, from Old French assigné, equivalent to assign + -ee.

senses: One who opposes, one who shows opposition.
examples: For example, after the opposer had objected to the opposee's plan to drive the car, the opposee suggested, "We can take turns driving the car."

senses: Having a dueling or Wild West character; wild and tough.
Carrying a gun as a weapon.
examples: So, every time he returned, convinced that he was still his old gunslinging self.

senses: To sort into such types (and identify them)
examples: Experiment 4 involved only morphotyping, and the results demonstrated the concentration-dependence of the subdivisions of morphotype 1.
Galls when found were inspected for inducers, collected separately in plastic bags when an insect or mite was found and were provisionally morphotyped (for organ, shape, colour and host plant).

senses: Located behind the peritoneum.
A hood, especially of a cloak; a capuche.
ety: Borrowed from Italian cappuccio. Doublet of capuche.
examples: Instead of a cappuccio, he wears a hat.

Within the Franciscans, a reformist group split off from the order in 1529 to restore the rigor of the original Rule of St. Francis, even to the point of emulating his four-cornered hood, called a cappuccio.

senses: An intelligent human-like reptile who walks on hind legs and speaks and dresses similar to humans.
A dull person (especially an old man) who is behind the times, holding antiquated, over-conservative views.
ety: Borrowed from Scots foggie, fogie (noun), perhaps derived from Scots foggie (“covered with moss or lichen; mossy", hence "old, antiquated, decrepit”, adjective), from Scots fog (“moss; lichen”), equivalent to fog (“moss”) + -y. Further origin uncertain. More at fog.

senses: A speaker who delivers the keynote speech of a conference.
The keynote speech itself.
A large sheet-metal stamping, often incorporating smaller welded stampings, that forms the floor of a large vehicle and the position of its external and structural panels.
Organised on a capitalist basis.
ety: From capitalist + -ic, probably after German kapitalistisch. Derived from Proto-Indo-European *káput (“head”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap-.

senses: The collection of union dues or other fees from employees via deductions from their wages.
The optional allocation of part of a citizen's income tax towards the presidential election campaign fund.
A tax on sales of agricultural goods in order to finance a generic commodity marketing program.
examples: Frye can help Seattles defense recognize formations, checkoffs and tendencies.

senses: A circular frame on which cadgers carry hawks for sale.
a biscuit consisting of currants squashed between layers of flaky pastry.
A kind of jacket worn by women.
ety: The jacket is named after Italian patriot Giuseppe Garibaldi, who wore a red shirt of similar appearance. The biscuit is also named after Garibaldi.

senses: A tropical American evergreen shrub, Bixa orellana; the lipstick tree; the fruit of the tree.
The seed of this tree used as a colouring or in Latin American cooking, containing bixin.
A fugitive orange-red dye obtained from this seed and fruit pulp through maceration and fermentation, used as textile dye and skin dye, containing bixin.
A believer in positivism.
ety: Perhaps borrowed from French positiviste. Equivalent to positive + -ist, after positivism.
examples: By discouraging what they conceive to be the weakness of their master, the English Positivists have broken the strength of their religion. A man who has faith must be prepared not only to be a martyr, but to be a fool.

senses: An embroidered tapestry from several central Asian countries.
ety: Borrowed from Persian سوزنی (suzani, “of or pertaining to needle”).
examples: She wore a coat made of old cloth from Uzbekistan called a suzani, which was faded black with embroidered red circles and yellow and white zigzags.

senses: A treeless grassland ecosystem covering extensive high areas of equatorial mountains, especially in South America.
